---
title: "Summary · Pico Identity"
---

## Key takeaways

- A Pico needs a cryptographic **identity** in addition to an **address**.
  An ECI answers "how do I reach this Pico here?"; a DID answers "which
  Pico is this?"
- Every Pico has a **did:webvh** — its public, resolvable passport — used
  for introduction and portability.
- Every relationship has its own pairwise **did:peer** — a private address
  used only for that relationship.
- Keeping relationship identities separate means one compromised
  relationship can be rotated or removed without affecting the others.
- The analogy to remember: **did:webvh = passport**, **did:peer = private
  address for one relationship**.
